title: Marketplaces and quick commerce
purpose: When a marketplace email, a short payout or a sudden sales drop lands and I do not know what it will cost, open Marketplaces to see the money at risk and fix it before the platform acts.
fires: the marketplace agency's monthly deck, the morning tour of 4 seller portals, the settlement spreadsheet nobody finishes, and the habit of looking only when sales drop.
not_for: a store that sells only on its own site, or lists a few products on one marketplace as a side test with a few orders a month.

jobs.job: When Amazon sends an account health warning on a Friday night, tell me what caused it, what it puts at risk and what to send back, so I do not lose the account and the money held in it
jobs.circumstance: Friday evening, a policy or performance email from Seller Central, 30 to 40 percent of revenue sits on that account, a 72 hour window to respond, nobody on the team has done this before

progress.functional: know the cause, the dollars at risk and the exact reply to send
progress.emotional: stop lying awake over a suspension that could end the channel
progress.social: show a partner or investor the account is handled, not left to luck

jobs.hire_today: a marketplace agency or a paid appeal writer, forum threads, or nothing until the email lands
jobs.fire: the late-night forum search, the rushed appeal writer, and the habit of looking at account health only after a warning

forces.push: one suspension freezes sales and the payout already owed
forces.pull: the cause, the at-risk dollars and a draft reply in one place, weeks before the platform acts
forces.habit: the agency has always handled Seller Central
forces.anxiety: what if the reply makes it worse; what if the warning signs were misread

jobs.little_hire: every week, and the hour any policy or performance email arrives

watch.metric: order defect rate and late shipment rate per marketplace against the platform limits, trailing 60 days
watch.source: Amazon Seller Central Account Health, Walmart Seller Center performance

drives.metric: days of marketplace selling lost to suspension or listing holds, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: order defect rate 0.8 percent against a 1 percent limit, not checked in 5 weeks. After: 3 causes fixed, rate at 0.3 percent within 30 days, 0 days suspended.
jobs.not_for: a brand with one marketplace listing and a few orders a month, where Seller Central's own email is enough

jobs.job: When the Amazon payout lands lower than the sales I saw, tell me where the gap went, fee by fee, so I can claim what is owed before the window closes
jobs.circumstance: payout day, the bank shows less than the sales report suggested, the settlement file has 2,000 lines, the bookkeeper cannot explain it

progress.functional: match each payout to its orders and name every fee, refund and hold
progress.emotional: stop feeling that the platform quietly takes money
progress.social: tell the bookkeeper and a partner exactly where the money went

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper, a reimbursement service on commission, or nothing because the settlement file is too hard to read
jobs.fire: the unread settlement file and the habit of trusting whatever lands in the bank

forces.push: money not claimed in time is gone for good
forces.pull: each gap named by cause with a claim ready to send
forces.habit: payouts are accepted as they arrive
forces.anxiety: what if I claim money that was never owed and annoy the platform

jobs.little_hire: every payout cycle, every 2 weeks

watch.metric: settlement shortfall: expected payout from order records minus actual payout, per settlement
watch.source: Amazon, Walmart and TikTok Shop settlement reports joined to orders

drives.metric: cash received from marketplaces per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the last 2 Amazon cycles paid $3,400 less than orders justify with no named cause. After: every gap tagged, $2,900 recovered within 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose marketplace sales are small enough that a few dollars of error is not worth an hour

jobs.job: When sales on a top product drop overnight while ads keep running, tell me if a reseller took the Buy Box (the main Add to Cart button), so I stop paying for their sales
jobs.circumstance: a morning check shows a top product's sales halved, ads still spending, no listing change on our side

progress.functional: know who holds the Buy Box on each advertised product and since when
progress.emotional: stop feeling robbed by my own ad budget
progress.social: give the agency or brand protection partner a clear case

jobs.hire_today: a marketplace manager checking by hand, a brand protection service, or nothing
jobs.fire: the manual spot check of each listing and the habit of blaming the algorithm

forces.push: every hour lost is ad money paying for a reseller's sale
forces.pull: a flag the day the Buy Box is lost on an advertised product, with the seller and price
forces.habit: we check listings when sales look odd
forces.anxiety: what if the flag is late and the damage is done anyway

jobs.little_hire: daily, and whenever a top product's sales drop

watch.metric: Buy Box win rate per advertised product, trailing 7 days
watch.source: Seller Central Business Reports or a Buy Box tracker

drives.metric: marketplace ad spend on products where we do not hold the Buy Box, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 advertised products below 60 percent Buy Box share, $2,100 a month of ads feeding resellers. After: ads paused on those within a day, share back above 90 percent in 3 weeks.
jobs.not_for: a brand that is the only seller on its listings and has Brand Registry locking them

jobs.job: When a best seller vanishes from search with no warning, tell me the same day that it was suppressed and why, so I fix it before a week of sales is gone
jobs.circumstance: a normal weekday, sales on one product fall to near 0, no email came, the listing still exists but shoppers cannot find it

progress.functional: know which listings are suppressed or blocked and the exact field or image at fault
progress.emotional: stop finding out a week late from the sales report
progress.social: look in control to the team, not caught out

jobs.hire_today: a marketplace manager who checks when sales drop, an agency, or nothing
jobs.fire: the weekly sales review as the alarm and the habit of assuming no email means no problem

forces.push: a suppressed best seller loses every sale until someone notices
forces.pull: same-day notice with the reason and the fix
forces.habit: sales reports have always been the warning
forces.anxiety: what if it floods me with small errors that do not matter

jobs.little_hire: daily, and after every listing or catalogue change

watch.metric: count of live listings suppressed or with an open error, daily
watch.source: Seller Central and Walmart Seller Center listing quality reports

drives.metric: marketplace revenue lost to suppressed days, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a top product suppressed for 6 days before anyone saw it. After: suppressions found within 24 hours, fixed within 48.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a few listings it already checks every day

progress.social: defend the channel mix to a partner with a number, not a revenue chart

jobs.hire_today: a founder spreadsheet updated twice a year, a marketplace agency deck showing sales, or nothing
jobs.fire: the twice-a-year margin spreadsheet and the habit of judging Amazon on its sales number

forces.push: stock and ad money keep flowing into products that may not pay
forces.pull: profit per unit per product, with the losers named before the shipment is booked
forces.habit: the sales number looks good enough
forces.anxiety: what if the fee math is wrong and I cut a product that works

jobs.little_hire: before every reorder, and at each monthly close

watch.metric: contribution margin per unit by marketplace and product, after all fees, trailing 30 days
watch.source: marketplace settlement and fee reports plus landed cost in the brand brain

drives.metric: total marketplace contribution margin per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $180,000 a month on Amazon, margin unknown. After: 6 products shown to lose $2 to $5 a unit, repriced or pulled within 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand that sells a handful of units on a marketplace to test it, not to earn from it

jobs.circumstance: mid-season, sales picking up, the restock report shows low cover, freight lead time is longer than the stock left

progress.functional: know which products run out first and the ship date that prevents it
progress.emotional: stop the dread of a stockout that costs weeks of rank
progress.social: tell the supplier and the forwarder a clear plan

jobs.hire_today: a marketplace manager with the restock report, a planning spreadsheet, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the weekly restock spreadsheet and the habit of reordering when the number looks low

forces.push: a stockout loses sales and the rank that took months to earn
forces.pull: days of cover per product against lead time, with the ship-by date

forces.anxiety: what if I ship too much and pay storage fees instead

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and when a product's sales speed jumps

watch.metric: top products with fewer days of stock at Amazon than restock lead time, daily
watch.source: Amazon Restock and inventory reports plus supplier lead time in the brand brain

drives.metric: stockout days on top products per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 of the top 20 products have under 30 days of cover and a 45 day restock. After: shipments booked, 0 top products out of stock next quarter.
jobs.not_for: a brand that ships its own marketplace orders from its own warehouse

progress.functional: know which campaigns spend above each product's break-even ad cost
progress.emotional: stop feeling the agency spends my money freely
progress.social: give the agency or freelancer a clear list to cut

jobs.hire_today: a marketplace agency or freelancer, or the platform's own sales-based return number
jobs.fire: the agency's sales-based ad report and the habit of judging ads on sales, not profit

forces.push: ad cost can eat the whole margin without anyone saying so
forces.pull: each campaign against the product's break-even, with the dollars above it

forces.anxiety: what if cutting ads drops organic rank too

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and when the ad bill jumps

watch.metric: ad cost as a share of ad sales per campaign against the product's break-even share, trailing 14 days
watch.source: Amazon Ads console, Walmart Connect, TikTok Shop ads

drives.metric: total marketplace ad cost as a share of marketplace sales, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 35 percent of Amazon ad spend sits above break-even. After: those campaigns cut or rebuilt, ad cost falls from 14 to 10 percent of sales in 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand not running any marketplace ads

jobs.job: When marketplace sales fall 20 percent and the agency says it is the season, tell me whether fewer people saw the product or fewer of them bought, so I fix the right thing
jobs.circumstance: a Monday review, sales down for 2 weeks, the agency has a story, nobody has split the drop

progress.functional: split the drop into page visits and buy rate per product
progress.emotional: stop guessing and arguing about causes
progress.social: hold the agency to a real answer

forces.push: weeks pass fixing the wrong thing
forces.pull: visits and buy rate per product against last month and last year

watch.metric: page visits and unit buy rate per top product, week over week
watch.source: Seller Central Business Reports

drives.metric: marketplace revenue per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 20 percent drop blamed on season. After: traced to a 35 percent fall in buy rate on 2 products after a price change, fixed in 10 days.

watch.source: marketplace review exports

forces.pull: one list ranked by dollars at risk

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 45 minutes a day across 4 portals, 2 costly notices missed last quarter. After: 10 minutes a day, 0 missed.
